ai.description: The Nicobarese Tree Frog (Rhacophoridae) reaches 5–6 cm. It is pale brown or yellowish with dark brown dorsal spots and a distinct white stripe along the upper lip. Large, fully webbed feet are present.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates insularis* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-brown lateral stripe extending from the snout through the eye, which is absent in similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: The Nicobarese tree frog inhabits tropical evergreen and moist deciduous forests, typically found at low to moderate elevations across the Nicobar Islands.
ai.behavior: The Nicobarese tree frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects among the foliage of its island habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates insularis* breeds during the monsoon, depositing a clutch of eggs within a foam nest attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates insularis* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands, an archipelago located in the Bay of Bengal within the Indian Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
ai.callDescription: The Nicobarese Tree Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "chick" notes, typically heard calling from vegetation near water bodies within its forest habitat.
